generation.hypothesis: Overcoming the strength-ductility trade-off in high entropy alloys can be achieved through the introduction of nanoscale interfaces and deformation twinning, which can be induced by severe plastic deformation and annealing processes.
generation.material_initial_state: as-cast or homogenized high entropy alloy
generation.intervention: severe plastic deformation (e.g. cryo-rolling) followed by annealing
generation.conditions: ambient temperature, initial strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1
generation.mechanism: strengthening via nanoscale interfaces and deformation twinning, derived from materials-science principles and supported by records node::W1971260269, node::W2968449032, node::W3015396998, and node::W4291396200
generation.predicted_outcome: improved strength-ductility synergy, with yield strength and ultimate tensile strength increasing by 50-100% and elongation to failure increasing by 20-50%
generation.baseline: conventional high entropy alloys without nanoscale interfaces and deformation twinning
generation.boundary: alloy composition, processing route, and test conditions
generation.uncertainty: effects of specific alloy composition and processing route on the strength-ductility trade-off, potential limitations of the severe plastic deformation and annealing processes

falsification_experiment.design: tensile testing of high entropy alloys with and without nanoscale interfaces and deformation twinning, using severe plastic deformation and annealing processes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the introduction of nanoscale interfaces and deformation twinning does not result in improved strength-ductility synergy, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: Can a novel hybrid-rolling process combining cryo-rolling and warm-rolling create a dual structural-compositional heterogeneous microstructure in an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy to achieve unprecedented strength-ductility synergy?. System: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA). Question: How can severe cryo-rolling followed by annealing be used to tailor heterogeneous microstructures and overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in brittle intermetallic-containing high entropy alloys?. System: CoCrFeNi2.1Nb0.2 high entropy alloy (FCC matrix with complex Laves phase particles). Processing: Homogenized ingots (1200 °C/24 h) were multi-pass cold- or cryo-rolled to 90% reduction in thickness (final thickness ~0.4 mm); cryo-rolling involved immersion in liquid N2 for 0.5 h before and after every pass; subsequent annealing at 800 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching.. Test conditions: Tensile tests conducted at ambient temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1 using dog-bone shaped specimens.. Own digest: Paper card. Question: How can the limited ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) be overcome to achieve ultra-ductility while maintaining high strength?. System: Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 (at%) eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases; industrial A357 casting aluminum alloy. Processing: Two cycles of 30% cold rolling followed by annealing at 1200 °C for 20 mins with water quenching; for A357: two cycles of 15% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins followed by two cycles of 30% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins. Test conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; in situ tensile tests in FE-SEM; loading-unloading-reloading tests for back stress measurement.
